hints.title: Range Replacement Cost Obstacle
hints.text: Testing every substring takes quadratic time. For a contiguous range of length L, how many character replacements are required to make all of its characters identical?

hints.title: Majority Frequency Invariant
hints.text: In any range, the fewest replacements needed equals the length minus the count of the most frequent character. The range is valid whenever length - max_frequency <= k.

hints.title: Dynamic Window Shrink Condition
hints.text: Expand a right boundary while counting character frequencies and updating max_freq. If window size - max_freq exceeds k, decrement the count of s[left] and increment left by 1. The maximum valid window size found is the answer.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of string s (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Single pass where left and right pointers each move at most N times; frequency map is bounded by 26 uppercase letters.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Checking all O(N^2) substrings and verifying whether the non-majority characters can be replaced within k edits takes O(26 * N^2) time, which causes time limit exceeded for N = 10^5.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining a running frequency map of size 26 allows dynamic window expansion and contraction in O(1) space and O(N) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Clear formulation of the valid window condition (length - max_freq <= k), knowing why max_freq does not need to be decremented when shrinking (or properly maintaining it), and achieving O(1) space.

solutions.approach: Dynamic Sliding Window with Max Frequency
